title: Homework 2 - Predicates and Quantifiers
text:
Sample Solutions
Note: Sample solutions are provided in order to help you learn. The purpose of these exercises is not to simply turn in the answers, but to take the time and effort to learn and understand the material. You are encouraged to work the problems first, then when you are satisfied that you have the correct answer, look at the sample solution and compare it with yours.

Sample Solution 2.1

Conditional and its contrapositive: \(p \rightarrow q \equiv \lnot q \rightarrow \lnot p\)
Inverse and Converse: \(\lnot p \rightarrow \lnot q \equiv q \rightarrow p\)
True. \(\lnot p \lor q\) is logically equivalent to \(p \rightarrow q\). We can show this using a truth table.
False. \(\lnot(p \rightarrow q)\) is NOT the same as $ p q$. We can show this using a truth table.
An equivalent statement to \(\lnot(p \rightarrow q)\) is \(\lnot (\lnot p \lor q)\), which we can simplify using De Morgan’s Laws to \(p \land \lnot q\).



Sample Solution 2.2

\(p \land r\)
Negated: \((\lnot p \lor \lnot r)\)
English: A rider is not older than 12 years old or is not taller than 48”.
\(q \lor r\)
Negated: \((\lnot q \land \lnot r)\)
English: A rider is not older than 18 years old and is not taller than 48”.
\(q \land \lnot r\)
Negated: \((\lnot q \lor r)\)
English: A rider is not older than 18 years old or is taller than 48”.



Sample Solution 2.3

Somebody is older than 21.
Everyone is older than 21.
Someone is not older than 21.
No one is older than 21.
Someone (or some person) is a student.
Everyone is a student.
There is no student.
There is someone who is not a student.
Not all people are non-students.
No one is a student.



Sample Solution 2.4

All friends are cool.
Someone is a friend and is cool.
Everyone is a friend and is cool.
Some friends are cool. (Better than ‘For some person, if that person is a friend, then that person is cool.’)
All students are from Nepal.
Someone, if he/she is a student then he/she is from Nepal. (Better than ’For some person, if that person is a student, then that student is from Nepal.)
Everyone is a student and is from Nepal.
Some student is from Nepal.



Sample Solution 2.5

\(\forall x\ C(x)\)
\(\forall x\ \lnot P(x)\)
\(\exists x\ (F(x) \land P(x))\)
\(\forall x\ (F(x) \rightarrow C(x))\)
\(\forall x\ C(x) \lor \exists x\ F(x)\)
\(\lnot \exists x\ C(x) \land \forall x\ F(x)\)
\(\exists x\ State(x) \land (\forall y\ State(y) \rightarrow \lnot ShareABorder(x, y))\)
\(\exists x\ is\_an\_Error(x) \rightarrow (\exists y\ is\_an\_error\_Message(y) \land is\_Displayed(y))\)
\([\forall x\ (is\_a\_Program(x) \rightarrow has\_been\_Scanned(x))] \land [\exists x\ (is\_a\_Program(x) \land has\_a\_Virus(x))]\)



Sample Solution 2.6


def is_even(x):
    return not(x % 2)

def forall(p, s):
    for x in s:
        if not p(x):
            return False
    return True



Sample Solution 2.7

def forsome(p, s):
    for x in s:
        if p(x):
            return True
    return False



Sample Solution 2.8

domain = list(range(-5, 6))

print(f'1. {forall(lambda x: x % 2, domain)}')
print(f'2. {forsome(lambda x: x % 2, domain)}')
print(f'3. {forall(lambda x: x < 0, domain)}')
print(f'4. {forsome(lambda x: x < 0, domain)}')
print(f'5. {forall(lambda x: x**2 - x != 1, domain)}')
print(f'6. {forall(lambda x: x**2 > 0, domain)}')
print(f'7. {forsome(lambda x: x**2 > 0, domain)}')
print(f'8. {forall(lambda x: x <= x + 1, domain)}')
print(f'9. {forsome(lambda x: x + x == 1, domain)}')
print(f'10. {forsome(lambda x: x + 2 == 1, domain)}')



Sample Solution 2.9

Every student asks some student a question.
Every student asks every student a question.
Some student asks at least one student a question.
Some student asks every student a question.
Every student is asked a question by some (or at least one) student.
Some student asks some student a question. (Another way to say the answer to 3.)



Sample Solution 2.10

\(\exists x \exists y \neg P(x,y)\)
\(\forall x \exists y \neg P(x,y)\)
\(\forall x \forall y \exists z P(x,y,z)\)
\(\exists x \forall y \exists z \neg P(x,y,z)\)
\(\forall x \forall y (\neg P(x,y) \lor \neg Q(x,y))\)
\(\exists x \exists y \forall z (P(x,y) \land \neg Q(y,z))\)



Sample Solution 2.11

\(\forall x\ H(x) \rightarrow V(x)\); negated is \(\exists x\ H(x) \land \lnot V(x)\) = ‘Some horse does not have hooves.’
\(\forall x\ H(x) \rightarrow \lnot F(x)\); negated is \(\exists x\ H(x) \land F(x) =\) ‘Some horse can fly’.
\(\forall x\ Bat(x) \rightarrow Blind(x)\); negated is \(\exists x\ Bat(x) \land \lnot Blind(x) =\) ‘Some bat is not blind’.
\(\forall x\ B(x) \rightarrow \lnot D(x)\); negated is \(\exists x\ B(x) \land D(x) =\) ‘Some bear can dance’.
\(\exists x\ Penguin(x) \land can\_Swim(x) \land can\_Catch\_Fish(x)\); negated is $x Penguin(x) can_Swim(x) can_Catch_Fish(x) = $ ‘Everything is either a non-penguin or a non-swimmer or a non-fish-catcher’ (or better: ‘No penguin can swim and catch fish’).



Sample Solution 2.12

The product of any two non-zero integers is non-zero and conversely, if the product of two numbers is non-zero, both numbers are non-zero. True
There is a number that when added to any number will result in a larger number. True. Pick any positive number for x.
There is a number that when added to any number will result in a smaller number. True. Pick any negative number for x.
There is a number that when added to any number will result in that same number. True. Pick x=0.
There are two numbers whose sum is equal to their product. True. Pick x=0 and y=0.

text:

isaac@applesdofall.org | My wikipedia page



Standing on the shoulders of giants


Laws of motion, gravitation, minting coins, disliking Robert Hooke



Cooling, power series, optics, alchemy, planetary motions, apples.




1654-1660 The King’s School, Grantham.
June 1661 - now Trinity College, Cambridge

Sizar

1669 Lectiones opticæ.
